title: PostHog offers a practical test for how much work to delegate to agents
friendlyTitle: A simple way to decide how much work an AI agent should do alone
summary: PostHog proposes grading agent autonomy by two properties of the task: how easily the result can be checked and how cheaply a mistake can be undone. Its four-level framework ranges from assistant mode to self-driving work, with deterministic tests and reversible changes enabling more delegation.
friendlySummary: PostHog says to ask two questions: can you easily check the work, and can you easily undo a mistake? The answers help you choose how closely a person should supervise the agent.
whyItMatters: Teams do not need one blanket policy for every agent. Classifying each workflow by verifiability and reversibility gives people a simple way to decide where human review, approval gates, tests and rollback should sit.
friendlyWhyItMatters: You can give agents more freedom on safe, testable jobs and keep people involved when mistakes would be difficult or expensive.
